lines.japanese: 朝の通学に関して言えば、一週間のうち月・水・木は比較的、楽な部類に入る。
lines.english: When it comes to the morning commute, Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are the easier days of the week.

lines.japanese: 好きな漫画雑誌に没入していれば、満員電車の人いきれもさほど気にならないうち終点へ運ばれているからだ。
lines.english: If I lose myself in a manga magazine I like, the train carries me to the last stop before the crush and heat of the packed car have much chance to bother me.

lines.japanese: しかし今朝は、何故だかいつもより誌面に身が入らなかった。
lines.english: But this morning, for some reason, I couldn't focus on the pages the way I usually did.

lines.japanese: なんだろう、据わりの悪いこの感覚は。
lines.english: What was this uneasy feeling?

lines.japanese: 絡みつくような気配。まるで誰かに観察されている気がして、ひどく落ちつかない。
lines.english: A presence that seemed to cling to me. I felt as though someone were watching me, and it left me terribly unsettled.

lines.japanese: 「くっ……つ、う……ふぁっ……」
lines.english: “Ngh... hhh... ah...”

lines.japanese: 密集したひとの塊から、異形の呻きにも似た荒い息遣いが聞こえる。
lines.english: From somewhere in the packed mass of bodies came ragged breathing, almost like the groans of some inhuman creature.

lines.japanese: なんだろう、寒気のするようなこの感覚は。
lines.english: What was this chilling feeling?

lines.japanese: 僕はなんとか『みぜＬＯＶＥる』に没入しようと、ことさら首を折って眼球と誌面との距離を狭めたりした。
lines.english: I tried to lose myself in *Mize LOVE-Ru*, hunching my neck even farther to bring my eyes closer to the page.

lines.japanese: しかし、ざらついた気配は拭いとれない。
lines.english: But I couldn't shake that prickling presence.

lines.japanese: ふと、成田君だった時間の記憶がよみがえった。
lines.english: Suddenly, a memory from the time I had been Narita returned to me.

lines.japanese: 僕を見詰める視線。あのときの粘ついた感覚に似ている。
lines.english: That gaze fixed on me. This felt like the same sticky sensation I'd had then.

lines.japanese: まさか何者かに見張られているわけでは、などと思いつつ、いっそ僕はおもてを上げた。
lines.english: Surely nobody was actually keeping watch on me, I thought, and finally raised my head.

lines.japanese: しかし、周囲を窺いかけたそのとき──
lines.english: But just as I started to look around—

lines.japanese: 「どぅおおおーっ！」
lines.english: “Whoooa!”

lines.japanese: ──列車が揺れて、ひとの壁がひしめきながら傾いた。
lines.english: —the train lurched, and the wall of people tipped over in a heaving crush.

lines.japanese: 「ひゃあっ！」
lines.english: “Eek!”

lines.japanese: 近くに立っていたソラ学制服の下級生が、僕と僕の雑誌を巻きこんで体重ごと圧しかかってくる。フルーティーな風が鼻腔を撫でた。
lines.english: A younger student in a Misora Academy uniform fell against me with all her weight, catching both me and my magazine. A fruity breeze brushed my nose.

lines.japanese: 僕は両手を支えに、筋力をふるって自分と後輩の体とを押しとどめた。
lines.english: I braced with both hands and strained to hold both myself and the girl upright.

lines.japanese: やがて負荷が消えた。ばたばたと乗客たちが体勢を立てなおす。車内はすぐに窮屈ながらの秩序を取りもどした。
lines.english: At last the pressure eased. The passengers bustled back into position, and the car soon recovered its cramped semblance of order.

lines.japanese: しかし例の下級生は、いまだ僕の胸に身を預けている。どうしたんだろう。融通の利かないエアコンのせいか、密着した制服の下に汗ばんだような体温を感じた。
lines.english: But the girl was still leaning against my chest. Was something wrong? Maybe it was the inflexible air conditioning, but through our pressed uniforms I could feel the damp warmth of her body.

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫？」
lines.english: “Are you all right?”

lines.japanese: 「あ！　いえ！　すみませんっ！」
lines.english: “Oh! Yes! I'm sorry!”

lines.japanese: 彼女は突然、僕の体を突きとばすように離れていった。
lines.english: She abruptly sprang away as though shoving me off.

lines.japanese: あとにはちょっと子供っぽいフルーツの香りと、表紙以下数百ページに折れ皺の付いた漫画雑誌が残った。
lines.english: All she left behind was a slightly childish fruit scent and a manga magazine creased through several hundred pages from the cover on down.

lines.japanese: 僕はそれを腰より低い位置へ落とした。隠さなければ、彼女はそれを自分の過失とみなして、ひどく気に病んでしまうような気がしたんだ。
lines.english: I lowered it out of sight below my waist. I had a feeling that if she saw the damage, she would blame herself and worry terribly over it.

lines.japanese: 「具合でも悪いの？」
lines.english: “Are you feeling sick or something?”

lines.japanese: 「い、いえ、その、へーきです……」
lines.english: “N-no, um, I'm fine...”

lines.japanese: 「そう。よかった」
lines.english: “Okay. Good.”

lines.japanese: それ以外とくに会話をするでもなかったが、僕らは満員電車の中で身動きもできず、ただ終点まで並んで立っていた。
lines.english: We didn't say anything else in particular. Unable to move in the crowded train, we simply stood side by side until the last stop.

lines.japanese: 僕の見間違えでなければ、この後輩の子は、このところ何度か見かけている。
lines.english: Unless I was mistaken, I had seen this younger girl several times lately.

lines.japanese: ひとの波に流されまいと必死でポールに抱きついている様が、なんだかちょっと可愛らしいと思っていた。
lines.english: I had thought there was something rather cute about the way she clung desperately to the pole so the tide of people wouldn't carry her off.

lines.japanese: 何故だかよほどその定位置が好きみたいで、僕のバッグを押しつぶしたり、僕の足を踏んづけてまで固執したこともあった。
lines.english: For some reason she seemed extremely attached to that particular spot. Once or twice, she had even crushed my bag or stepped on my foot to keep it.

lines.japanese: 思えばずっと前から、この車両に乗りあわせていたかもしれない──ちょっと判然としないけれど。
lines.english: Come to think of it, she might have been riding in this car for ages—though I couldn't say for sure.

lines.japanese: 名も知らぬ誰かと無言で過ごす十数分という時間を、窮屈も焦燥も抱かずいられたのは、僕と一緒になってくれた他の僕たちのお陰かもしれない。
lines.english: Perhaps I could spend those dozen-odd silent minutes beside a nameless stranger without feeling cramped or impatient thanks to the other selves who had joined me.

lines.japanese: 強さや器用さを与えてくれた、頼もしい兄弟。
lines.english: My dependable brothers, who had given me their strength and skill.

lines.japanese: 「あの、雑誌……」
lines.english: “Um, your magazine...”

lines.japanese: 途中、か細い声が何度か聞こえた気もしたけれど、僕が首を曲げると、決まって彼女は下を向いて石のように固まっていた。
lines.english: I thought I heard her faint voice a few times along the way, but whenever I turned to look, she would stare down and go rigid as stone.

lines.japanese: 独り言の癖がある子なのかもしれない。隣りに立つその制服姿を盗み見て、ちょっと微笑ましい気持ちになった。
lines.english: Maybe she had a habit of talking to herself. I stole a glance at the uniformed girl beside me and found it rather endearing.

lines.japanese: それにしても、さっきまで感じられていた、あの粘りつくような気配はなんだったんだろう。
lines.english: Still, what had that clinging presence I felt before been?

lines.japanese: 蒸し暑い車内からホームへ降りたった僕は、冬の朝の冷たさに感謝する。
lines.english: Stepping from the sweltering car onto the platform, I gave thanks for the cold winter morning.

lines.japanese: 折れまがった雑誌をバッグへしまいながら、改札へと向かう。
lines.english: I tucked the bent magazine into my bag and headed for the ticket gates.

lines.japanese: 今日はお気に入りの漫画が一本しか読めなかった。今週の『みぜＬＯＶＥる』はどんな展開だろう。前回は水着姿の鴨志田さんがモロヘイヤの怪物に絡めとられて大変なことになっていたけれど──
lines.english: I had only managed to read one of my favorite manga today. What would happen in this week's *Mize LOVE-Ru*? Last time, Kamoshida was in her swimsuit and a molokhia monster had tangled her up in a terrible predicament—

lines.japanese: 「２Ｂの林田美咲と申します！　先程は失礼いたしました！」
lines.english: “My name is Misaki Hayashida, from Class 2-B! I apologize for what happened earlier!”

lines.japanese: それはあまりに突然のことだった。
lines.english: It came so completely out of nowhere.

lines.japanese: 決して鴨志田さんのあられもない姿に思いを馳せていたわけではないけれど、いきなり現れて頭を下げだした後輩の姿に、僕は呆然としてしまった。
lines.english: I certainly hadn't been picturing Kamoshida in her indecent predicament, but when the younger girl suddenly appeared and bowed to me, I could only stare blankly.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、さっきの。いいよ、そんな」
lines.english: “Oh, you're the girl from before. It's fine, really.”

lines.japanese: 「いえっ！　ほんとに！　すみませんでした！」
lines.english: “No! Truly! I’m very sorry!”

lines.japanese: 腰を折ったまま、はっきりした声でいう。驚くぐらい礼儀正しくて丁寧な子だ。
lines.english: Still bent at the waist, she spoke in a clear voice. She was astonishingly polite and proper.

lines.japanese: 「それではっ！」
lines.english: “Then, if you'll excuse me!”

lines.japanese: しかし、やっと顔を上げたと思ったら、そのまま逃げるようにすたすたと立ちさってしまった。
lines.english: But the moment she finally lifted her head, she hurried off as though fleeing.

lines.japanese: せっかくだから学校まで一緒に、なんて図々しい考えが頭をよぎったのだけど、やっぱり漫画みたいな展開にはならなかった。ちょっと残念。
lines.english: For a moment I had the presumptuous thought that, since we were here, we might walk to school together. But things didn't turn out like a manga after all. A little disappointing.

lines.japanese: 僕は部活動と三年間無縁だったから、後輩の友人というものが欲しかったんだ。ましてやあんな可愛らしい子だったら……なんて言ったら渡来さんに怒られるかな。
lines.english: I had gone all three years without joining a club, so I had always wanted a younger friend. And if she happened to be as cute as that... Would Watarai get angry if she heard me say that?

lines.japanese: ラッシュアワーの混雑の中、あたふたと遠ざかる背中を眺めながら思った。
lines.english: I watched the girl's flustered retreat through the rush-hour crowd and thought.

lines.japanese: もし明日も彼女と同じ車両に乗りあわせたら、今度はこちらから声をかけてみようか。もう知らない仲じゃないんだし、名前ぐらいは聞かせてもらっても──
lines.english: If we happened to ride in the same car again tomorrow, perhaps I would speak to her first. We weren't complete strangers anymore, so surely I could at least ask her name—
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: ──そういえばあの子、さっき名乗っていた気がする。なんといったか。
lines.english: —come to think of it, I thought she had introduced herself just now. What had she said?

lines.japanese: たしか……しだ、しだ、かもしだ？　違う、それは漫画のキャラクターだ。はやしだ？　たぶん違う、かもしだに引っ張られてるだけだ。
lines.english: It was... shida, shida... Kamoshida? No, that was the manga character. Hayashida? Probably not. I was just getting stuck on Kamoshida.

lines.japanese: 駄目だ、思いだせない。
lines.english: No use. I couldn't remember.

lines.japanese: 彼女は不意に振りかえったが、僕の視線にぶつかると、びっくりして恥ずかしそうにぺこぺこ頭を下げていた。
lines.english: She suddenly looked back. When our eyes met, she startled and bowed again and again in embarrassment.

lines.japanese: 面白い子だなあ。
lines.english: What an interesting girl.

lines.japanese: 行ってらっしゃい、ひそかな友達──名前も知らない女生徒Ａさん。
lines.english: Off you go, my secret friend—Miss Nameless Schoolgirl A.
